variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A large language model (LLM) is a neural network trained to predict tokens in language. By repeating that prediction one token at a time, it can draft text, summarize documents, answer questions, transform structured data, and help call software tools.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Learn the four layers of an LLM system”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Tokenizer
pairs.detail: A tokenizer maps text into vocabulary units.
pairs.explanation: A tokenizer maps text into vocabulary units. A token may be a word, part of a word, punctuation, or bytes; token count is therefore not the same as word count.

pairs.label: Model weights
pairs.explanation: Parameters are learned numeric weights. They store statistical behavior from training, not an inspectable database of verified facts.

pairs.label: Context window
pairs.detail: The context contains the tokens retained for one request.
pairs.explanation: The context contains the tokens retained for one request. Material omitted or truncated from that window cannot be directly attended to.

pairs.label: Decoder
pairs.detail: The decoder turns model scores into a next-token choice.
pairs.explanation: The decoder turns model scores into a next-token choice. Temperature and sampling change selection behavior; they do not add knowledge.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. An LLM generates a likely continuation from its model weights and retained context.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Trace how one response is generated”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Tokenize the request
pairs.detail: Convert instructions, user text, evidence, and prior turns into token IDs under one versioned tokenizer.
pairs.explanation: Convert instructions, user text, evidence, and prior turns into token IDs under one versioned tokenizer.

pairs.label: Build contextual states
pairs.detail: Transformer layers let each position combine relevant information from the visible prefix while respecting the model's attention rules.
pairs.explanation: Transformer layers let each position combine relevant information from the visible prefix while respecting the model's attention rules.

pairs.label: Score the vocabulary
pairs.detail: The model emits one score, or logit, for each possible next token.
pairs.explanation: The model emits one score, or logit, for each possible next token. Softmax converts the scores into a probability distribution.

pairs.label: Choose and repeat
pairs.detail: Greedy decoding selects the highest probability; sampling may select another allowed token.
pairs.explanation: Greedy decoding selects the highest probability; sampling may select another allowed token. The result is appended and the cycle continues.

pairs.label: Small general model
pairs.detail: Use for bounded extraction, classification, rewriting, and routine chat when representative tests show enough quality.
pairs.explanation: Use for bounded extraction, classification, rewriting, and routine chat when representative tests show enough quality. Lower latency and cost often improve the complete product.

pairs.label: Large general model
pairs.detail: Use when difficult reasoning or broad language coverage creates measured task value that justifies higher latency, token cost, and capacity pressure.
pairs.explanation: Use when difficult reasoning or broad language coverage creates measured task value that justifies higher latency, token cost, and capacity pressure.

pairs.label: Hosted model
pairs.detail: The provider owns serving infrastructure, while you still own data policy, prompt behavior, evaluation, dependency risk, and complete task economics.
pairs.explanation: The provider owns serving infrastructure, while you still own data policy, prompt behavior, evaluation, dependency risk, and complete task economics.

pairs.label: Self-hosted model
pairs.detail: Useful for residency, customization, or offline constraints when the team can own accelerators, batching, memory, scaling, upgrades, and incident response.
pairs.explanation: Useful for residency, customization, or offline constraints when the team can own accelerators, batching, memory, scaling, upgrades, and incident response.
